name: SOLID Principles, Clean Architecture & KISS
tagline: Pointing source dependencies inward via Dependency Inversion and Ports & Adapters on core domains, while keeping simple CRUD KISS-compliant.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of SOLID, Clean Architecture, and KISS—from preventing inverted dependency leakage to enforcing boundaries with ArchUnit/import-linter.

spark.summary: SOLID, Clean Architecture, and KISS balance extensibility against simplicity: SOLID guides modular boundaries and dependency direction, Clean Architecture isolates domain rules from frameworks and databases, and KISS prevents premature abstraction.
spark.keyTakeaway: Apply Dependency Inversion at architectural boundaries (DB, HTTP, queues) while keeping internal domain logic direct and KISS-compliant.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **SOLID** is five modular design heuristics: **SRP** (one cohesive actor/reason to change), **OCP** (extend via new code without editing core switches), **LSP** (subtypes honor base contracts), **ISP** (focused role interfaces).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Inward Dependency Direction: Domain Core <- Application Ports <- Infra Adapters (Domain Core (Pure) -> Domain Ports (ISP) -> PostgresAdapter -> StripeAdapter); Pragmatic KISS vs. Clean Boundary Decision Flow (NEW FEATURE -> VERTICAL SLICE -> HEXAGONAL PORT).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose architectural ceremony proportional to domain complexity. Combine Clean Architecture on the write path (`Order` invariants + `CheckoutUseCase` + Ports) with lightweight direct SQL projections on read-only endpoints (`GET /orders/{id}`), guarded by automated CI import checks.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore how SOLID and Clean Architecture apply to LLD systems, Dependency Injection, and DDD Aggregates.

learningJourney.title: What are SOLID, Clean Architecture & KISS
learningJourney.explanation:
**SOLID** is five modular design heuristics: **SRP** (one cohesive actor/reason to change), **OCP** (extend via new code without editing core switches), **LSP** (subtypes honor base contracts), **ISP** (focused role interfaces), and **DIP** (high-level policy depends on abstractions, not concrete I/O).

**Clean / Hexagonal Architecture** scales DIP to the system: dependencies point *inward* toward pure domain rules, never *outward* toward SQL, HTTP, or vendor SDKs. **KISS** is the essential counterweight—every abstraction pays cognitive rent and must earn its keep.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how SOLID, Clean Architecture & KISS works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Coupling Rots Codebases (and How Ports & Adapters Save Migrations)
learningJourney.explanation: Codebases rot in two opposite ways: 'Big Ball of Mud' handlers mixing SQL, Stripe SDKs, and business rules in 250-line methods, or 'Enterprise FizzBuzz' wrapping 3-field CRUD in 4 interface layers. Applying DIP at I/O boundaries lets core domain logic survive full database migrations untouched.

sectionDiagram.title: Inward Dependency Direction: Domain Core <- Application Ports <- Infra Adapters
sectionDiagram.summary: Source-code dependencies point inward: infrastructure adapters implement domain-owned ports, never the reverse.

ideas.title: Hexagonal Architecture Saved a Ledger Migration
ideas.description: Because `SettlementEngine` only imported a domain `LedgerPort` interface (zero `@Entity` annotations), migrating from PostgreSQL to DynamoDB took 3 weeks in `DynamoLedgerAdapter` with zero edits to settlement rules.

ideas.title: Fixing an LSP Violation via ISP
ideas.description: `ReadOnlyS3Store` threw `UnsupportedOperationException` on `put()`, crashing workers expecting `BlobStore`. Splitting into `ReadableBlobStore` and `WritableBlobStore` caught invalid assignments at compile time.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Why Coupling Rots Codebases under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where Clean Architecture Belongs (and Where KISS / Vertical Slices Win)
learningJourney.explanation: Reserve full Ports & Adapters for the ~20% of your system holding complex invariants, money movement, or volatile external integrations.

comparison.choice: Use Clean/Hexagonal: Core Domain & Volatile Integrations
benefits: Millisecond unit tests, zero framework lock-in, safe DB/vendor swaps.
costs: DTO mapping boilerplate across HTTP -> Command -> Domain -> DB boundaries.

comparison.choice: Use KISS / Vertical Slice: Simple CRUD & Read Queries
benefits: Direct SQL/jOOQ/SQLAlchemy projection queries avoid 4x ceremony and fight zero joins.
costs: N/A—simplicity is a feature when no complex invariants exist.

comparison.choice: Avoid: Tight SIMD / Game-Physics Hot Loops
benefits: Direct value/struct loops preserve CPU cache locality.
costs: Virtual interface dispatch adds indirection overhead.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How to Enforce Boundaries in CI with ArchUnit / `import-linter`
learningJourney.explanation: Architectural rules decay under deadline pressure unless automated as CI fitness functions. Use **ArchUnit** (Java) or **`import-linter`** (Python) to fail builds if `domain` imports `infrastructure`, `sqlalchemy`, or `springframework`. Place `@Transactional` at the Application UseCase boundary, not inside individual repositories.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```ini
# pyproject.toml — import-linter contract enforcing Clean Architecture in CI (Python)
[tool.importlinter]
root_package = my_app

[[tool.importlinter.contracts]]
name = "Domain must stay pure"
type = forbidden
source_modules = ["my_app.domain"]
forbidden_modules = ["my_app.infrastructure", "sqlalchemy", "fastapi", "httpx"]
```
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Clean Architecture vs. Vertical Slice vs. Transaction Script
learningJourney.explanation: Choose architectural ceremony proportional to domain complexity.

benefits: Maximum testability and infrastructure isolation for core domains.
costs: High boilerplate if cargo-culted onto simple `GET /health` or CRUD endpoints.

benefits: Groups each feature's handler, validation, and query together with minimal cross-layer indirection.
costs: Can duplicate domain logic if rich invariants span multiple slices.

benefits: Fastest to write and debug for simple scripts and admin CRUD.
costs: Degrades into a Big Ball of Mud if complex state machines accumulate.

knowledgeCheck.question: A `ReadOnlyS3Store` subclass extends `BlobStore` and throws `UnsupportedOperationException` when `put(key, bytes)` is called, crashing background workers at runtime. Which two SOLID principles are violated, and what is the fix?

options.text: Liskov Substitution (LSP) and Interface Segregation (ISP); split `BlobStore` into `ReadableBlobStore` and `WritableBlobStore`
options.feedback: Correct: subtypes must honor base contracts (LSP), and focused role interfaces (ISP) prevent read-only stores from implementing `put()`.
Suppressing warnings does not fix runtime contract violations.

options.text: KISS; merge all storage methods into one `GodStore` class
